Kwara State Governor, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, has approved the promotion of 5,956 teaching and non-teaching staff of the State Universal Basic Education Board, with the financial benefits taking effect from October 2026. The approval, according to a statement obtained by The PUNCH on Friday, followed a computer-based test conducted by the board earlier in the month for eligible employees. The SUBEB oversees the implementation of basic education programmes in public primary and junior secondary schools in Kwara State. Staff promotions are part of the public service career progression process, while regular training and improved welfare are among the measures used to support teachers and strengthen the delivery of basic education. Speaking on the development, the board’s Executive Chairman, Raheem Adaramaja, disclosed that the affected workers will receive their promotion letters through education secretaries in their respective local government areas. The chairman further said that the state government had also addressed promotion arrears inherited from the previous administration. “This includes the arrears of SUBEB staff promotions inherited from the previous administration. The Governor has long settled 345% of salary arrears accrued from instalment payments inherited from the past administration,” he said. Adaramaja said the government was pursuing improvements in public basic education within available resources, adding that teachers’ welfare was important to improving pupils’ performance. “The government is taking every step within available resources to drive efficient performance of students in public basic schools. This is partly achievable when their teachers are well taken care of,” he said. He thanked the governor for approving the 2026 computer-based promotion exercise and for providing other support to the board. Toheeb Omotayo
